source.title: Lower Bounds for Unrestricted Boolean Circuits: Open Problems

accepted.question_text: Can gate elimination alone be used to prove a 4n lower bound on the number of gates needed to compute some n-input Boolean function by a Boolean circuit?

evidence.quote: Can one at least prove a 4n lower bound using gate elimination?

accepted.question_text: For Boolean functions with multiple outputs, can one prove lower bounds that are stronger than the currently known bounds for single-output Boolean functions?

evidence.quote: Can one prove stronger lower bounds for functions with multiple outputs?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove a 5n lower bound for the Boolean-circuit size of an n-input, n-output Boolean function, that is, for some function in B_{n,n}?

evidence.quote: We use Bn,m to denote the set of all Boolean functions with n inputs and m outputs.
How to prove a 5n lower bound for a function from Bn,n?

accepted.question_text: Is there a non-gate-elimination method for proving lower bounds for unrestricted Boolean circuits that can be extended past the current 2n barrier?

evidence.quote: Are there approaches other than gate elimination for proving lower bounds for unrestricted circuits.
Can any of these non-gate-elimination methods be extended to get stronger than 2n lower bounds?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a symmetric Boolean function whose circuit size grows superlinearly with n, where symmetric means that the output depends only on the number of 1 bits among the inputs?

evidence.quote: Can one prove a superlinear lower bound for a symmetric function (i.e., a function whose output depends on the sum of input bits only)? In fact, one cannot:
any symmetric function can be computed by a circuit of size 4.5n + o(n) as shown by Demenkov et al. [10].

accepted.question_text: What is the Boolean-circuit size of SUM_n, the multi-output Boolean function that returns the binary encoding of the sum of the n input bits?

evidence.quote: Note that the multi-output function SUMn ∈ Bn,⌈log2(n+1)⌉ that outputs the binary encoding of the sum of n input bits is not easier than any symmetric function f ∈ Bn:
What is the circuit size of SUMn?

accepted.question_text: Can one improve on brute-force search for the satisfiability problem for Boolean circuits of size 4n on n inputs?

evidence.quote: Can one improve the brute force search for the satisfiability problem on circuits of size 4n?

accepted.question_text: If there is a non-trivial satisfiability algorithm for Boolean circuits of size cn on n inputs, does that imply cn lower bounds for Boolean-circuit complexity?

evidence.quote: Do non-trivial satisfiability algorithms for circuits of size cn imply cn lower bounds?

accepted.question_text: Suppose one starts with a Boolean function on a constant number of inputs that already has high circuit complexity. Can one systematically turn it into a family of n-input Boolean functions whose circuit complexity stays high, rather than losing hardness through the mass production effect?
accepted.context_brief: Producing hard families from small hard functions

evidence.quote: Can one take a sufficiently hard function with constant number of inputs and cook out of it a family of functions of high circuit complexity?

accepted.question_text: Which Boolean functions avoid the mass production effect, meaning that for the function r × f obtained by applying f to r independent input blocks, the circuit size of r × f is not much smaller than r times the circuit size of f?

evidence.quote: For a positive integer r and a function f ∈ Bn, by r ×f we denote a function from Brn,r that applies f to r independent blocks of size n. We say that a mass production effect occurs for f when gates(r × f) is (much) smaller than r · gates(f).
What are the functions avoiding mass production effect?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove superlinear lower bounds for Boolean circuits whose depth is logarithmic in the number of inputs, that is, O(log n)?

evidence.quote: Can we at least prove superlinear lower bounds on circuits of logarithmic (i.e., O(log n)) depth?

accepted.question_text: Can one prove superlinear lower bounds for linear Boolean circuits that use only parity gates, especially for multi-output linear maps of the form f(x) = Ax over {0,1}?

evidence.quote: Can we at least prove superlinear lower bounds for circuits consisting of parity gates only? This question makes sense for multi-output functions. Specifically, let us focus on functions of the form f(x) = Ax where A ∈ {0, 1}n×n.

accepted.question_text: Can one prove multiplicative-complexity lower bounds mc(f) ≥ n, or even mc(f) ≥ (1 + ε)n, for explicit Boolean functions f, where mc(f) is the minimum number of AND-type gates needed to compute f when XOR-type gates are treated as free?

evidence.quote: What if some gates are given for free? Basically, each gate in a binary Boolean circuit is either an XOR-type gate ... or an AND-type gate ...
The minimum number of AND-type gates required to compute f is known as multiplicative complexity of f, mc(f).
Strangely enough, this is the strongest known lower bound: we do not know how to prove mc(f) ≥ n, let alone proving mc(f) ≥ (1 + )n.
